items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-16
items.q: New York didn't jump till after 25, or after Jack Peaygarden and Nichols, and all them boys coming in and big.

ctx.x: You hear so much about the Roaring Twenties, I didn't live it. Could you tell me a little bit about it?

Well, I can tell you, uh, a little, a little far back than that. I'm sure you could. Well, but this is a little far back than that. I'll say first and, uh, I guess before I joined Joe Oliver, you know, I was in New Orleans during the days, uh, of, uh, dance bands, and, uh, I noticed, uh, there were such things at the club where the members would die, you know? Yeah. And the musicians that started this up in the twenties, all from New Orleans, uh, what do you call me? Yeah. So if a member died, and, uh, they lay…
Yeah, well, do you feel that it used to swing more in the good old days, or is that just talking and swinging right now?
